objective: Build a multivariate forensic fingerprint capable of distinguishing implementations of the same censorship/DPI mechanism, with priority comparison Cuba vs MegaCom/known-PROTEI environment vs Russia/TSPU and multiple non-PROTEI controls.

evidence_hierarchy.name: POLITICAL_EVENT_COINCIDENCE
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: Protest/election timing alone has zero vendor-attribution value.

evidence_hierarchy.name: SERVICE_FAILURE
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: Selective outage is useful operationally but not implementation-specific.

evidence_hierarchy.name: GENERIC_MECHANISM
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: DNS poison, TLS timeout, RST after ClientHello, packet drop, throttling. Often shared by unrelated systems.

evidence_hierarchy.name: NETWORK_LOCALIZATION
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: ASN/hop/on-path vs upstream localization. Necessary to avoid attributing upstream censorship to the access ISP.

evidence_hierarchy.name: STATE_MACHINE_AND_PARSER_DNA
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: Residual timers, tuple scope, reset semantics, fragmentation, checksum/sequence validation, protocol-version/parser quirks.

evidence_hierarchy.name: MULTI_PROTOCOL_COHERENCE
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: Same unusual behavior across TLS, QUIC, HTTP, IP fragmentation and/or certificate parsing.

evidence_hierarchy.name: DEVICE_OR_SOFTWARE_IDENTITY
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: Banner, package name, process name, management interface, config syntax, unique TLS client fingerprint from middlebox, firmware/product artifact.

evidence_hierarchy.name: CONTROL_CHANNEL
evidence_hierarchy.meaning: Observed management/update path or authoritative deployment evidence tying device to operator/vendor/control plane.

packet_injection_morphology: Initial TTL of injected RST/SYN-ACK/block response
IP ID pattern: constant, monotonic, random, zero, per-flow
Number of injected packets per trigger
state_machine: Whether additional blocked packets reset the timer
Whether source-port rotation escapes residual state
Whether destination-port rotation escapes residual state
State timeout before first application payload
parser_semantics: TCP stream reassembly vs single-packet parsing
topology: Hop localization using TTL-limited trigger packets
cross_protocol_policy: HTTP Host and TLS SNI overlap
control_plane_dynamics: Identical rule changes across independent networks
Firmware/version transition correlated with behavior change

discriminators: Unique IP-fragment state management: buffers incomplete fragments but forwards fragments individually rather than normalizing them into one packet.
Subsequent fragments inherit/are rewritten to the TTL of fragment zero.
Maximum of 45 fragments for one IP packet; duplicate or overlapping fragments can cause the whole queue to be dropped.
TSPU is in-path and stateful; large-scale measurement placed many devices close to subscribers, often within two hops.

Current QUIC censorship is SNI-dependent and packet-drop based; public 2026 work reports residual state lasting about 420 seconds on a 4-tuple and retriggering/restarting on another blocked QUIC Initial.
Current QUIC parser behavior distinguishes QUIC v1 from v2 and differs from the GFW under crafted payload layouts.
Public research reports near-complete correspondence of TLS-SNI and QUIC-SNI blocklists, a useful cross-protocol coherence signal.
TCP/ESNI and fully encrypted traffic residual censorship commonly 120 or 180 seconds.
Additional packets generally do not reset the residual timer.
QUIC SNI censorship uses about 180 seconds of residual blocking and a 3-tuple keyed on source IP, destination IP and destination port; source-port changes do not trivially escape it.
QUIC filter does not reassemble Initial data split across multiple UDP datagrams in the documented implementation.
Geneva experiments show distinctive parser laxity such as accepting malformed checksums/sequence semantics in some censorship paths.
Residual/protocol-state window about 60 seconds in studied filter.
Additional nonconforming traffic resets the timer.
No TCP reassembly in the documented protocol filter.
Does not verify packet checksums in the studied path.
Unidirectional behavior for flows originating in Iran.
Per-flow packet-count behavior can be exhausted by crafted repeated handshake packets.
HTTP/TLS censorship persists roughly 30 seconds on the same 4-tuple in published measurement.
Injected responses show distinctive IP-ID and initial-TTL patterns.
Repeated probes may trigger anti-measurement behavior from the censor, which is itself a behavioral fingerprint.
When interception is triggered, the middlebox itself connects to the origin server and exposes a TLS ClientHello fingerprint distinct from the RIPE Atlas probe.
Researchers reported the intercepting middlebox TLS fingerprint as virtually unseen in ordinary Internet traffic, making outbound-middlebox TLS fingerprinting a high-specificity technique.
Public EcoSGE/EcoDPI documentation states HTTPS URL filtering uses SNI to break/drop a connection to a forbidden resource.
If SNI is absent, the documented behavior passes the request transparently.
Documentation also describes checking the incoming server certificate and dropping the connection when denied content is identified in the certificate.
Public product material confirms signature/statistical application detection, URL categorization/blocking, redirect capability, bandwidth policy and integration with external policy applications.
MegaCom is a confirmed historical PROTEI_DPI deployment; later content filtering combined Entensys classification with PROTEI_DPI policy enforcement.
Public material located in this audit does not disclose a vendor-unique packet injection/state-machine signature comparable to TSPU fragmentation or GFW residual semantics.

specificity_ranking.reason: Useful when stable across many flows and networks, but implementations/configurations can change.

specificity_ranking.feature: Residual timer + tuple scope + reset semantics
specificity_ranking.reason: Encodes internal state-machine design and is more discriminating.
Reveals implementation quirks difficult to match accidentally.

specificity_ranking.feature: TSPU 45-fragment limit + TTL inheritance + overlap behavior
specificity_ranking.reason: Published as a fairly unique remote TSPU fingerprint.
Can directly fingerprint the software stack if censor actively proxies to origin.
Direct control-plane evidence; strongest attribution bridge.

phase_0_controls: Use identical controlled destination servers and identical client payloads from each vantage point.
Collect matched nonblocked-domain controls before and after every trigger.
Record traceroute/AS path and provider status to exclude routing/service incidents.
phase_1_packet_morphology: Capture full bidirectional PCAP around blocked and control handshakes.
Measure RST TTL, IPID, flags, seq, ack, window, TCP options, checksum, timestamps and trigger-to-RST latency.
Repeat at least 100 times per vantage/domain to distinguish stable fingerprint from network noise.
phase_2_state_machine: After one censorship trigger, probe at 1, 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, 180, 300, 420 and 600 seconds.
Rotate source port, destination port, destination IP and source IP independently to infer tuple scope.
Send repeated blocked triggers to test whether the timer restarts.
phase_3_parser_fuzz: Split ClientHello across TCP segments at controlled offsets.
Send IP fragments including duplicates and overlaps under a lawful controlled test server.
Vary fragment count up to and beyond 45 to test the known TSPU boundary.
Vary TTL across fragment zero and later fragments to test TSPU TTL inheritance.
Test invalid checksum, seq/ack, unusual flags and TCP data-offset where lawful and safe.
Vary TLS 1.2/1.3, SNI presence, ciphersuite ordering and extensions.
Test SNI absent but certificate SAN/CN containing a blocked name to probe EcoDPI-documented certificate behavior.
phase_4_quic: Split QUIC Initial across datagrams where implementation allows.
Test residual state duration and tuple scope.
Test whether another blocked Initial resets residual state.
Compare TLS-SNI and QUIC-SNI blocklists on an identical domain corpus.
phase_5_localization: Use TTL-limited trigger packets/CenTrace-style methods to identify the first hop at which behavior changes.
For MegaCom, explicitly distinguish local AS50223 enforcement from AS12389 Rostelecom upstream enforcement.
For Cuba, localize AS27725 behavior and compare geography/hop placement across provinces/vantage points.
phase_6_identity: Probe only publicly exposed lawful management/banner surfaces for vendor/software identifiers.
Search operator/vendor deployment documents, tender records, archived manuals, engineer CVs and integration material for exact product/version names.
If the censor performs origin-side proxy connections, derive its TLS ClientHello/JA3/JA4-style implementation fingerprint from a controlled server.

decision_logic.CUBA_PROTEI_WEAK_SUPPORT: Cuba and known-PROTEI vantage share only generic RST/timeout/SNI behavior.
decision_logic.CUBA_PROTEI_MODERATE_SUPPORT: They additionally share stable packet morphology AND residual-state semantics that differ from non-PROTEI controls.
decision_logic.CUBA_PROTEI_STRONG_SUPPORT: They additionally share parser-fuzz quirks, tuple/timer behavior and topology-localized implementation fingerprint across repeated tests.
decision_logic.CUBA_PROTEI_DEVICE_LEVEL: A direct product/banner/config/package/origin-TLS fingerprint or deployment record identifies PROTEI_DPI at the Cuban censorship point.
decision_logic.TSPU_LIKE_STRONG_SUPPORT: A foreign network reproduces the composite TSPU fragmentation fingerprint (45-fragment ceiling, overlap/duplicate queue behavior, fragment-zero TTL inheritance) plus compatible state/topology behavior.
decision_logic.REMOTE_RUSSIAN_CONTROL: Still NOT established without an observed/authoritative control-channel bridge. Device similarity or Russian vendor origin is insufficient.

audit_conclusions: The current strongest remote fingerprint for TSPU is not RST behavior but its unusual IP-fragment state management combined with TTL rewriting and topology localization.

Residual-censorship timers and keying semantics are high-value differentiators: TSPU (~420 s/resettable/4-tuple in current QUIC study), GFW (~120/180 s generally non-resetting; QUIC ~180 s/3-tuple), Iran (~60 s resettable in studied protocol filter), Turkmenistan (~30 s/4-tuple in published study).

Parser-fuzz response matrices can classify censorship devices because commercial devices from the same vendor exhibit strongly correlated behavior; published CenFuzz work found same-vendor devices clustering tightly.
A single packet-level mechanism should never be treated as vendor identity. Attribution should require a vector of independent features from state, parser, topology and identity layers.
The Cuba↔PROTEI hypothesis remains scientifically open, but the next evidence should come from low-level state/parser fingerprints or direct product identity, not more reports of SNI/RST blocking.
epistemic_firewall: same parser behavior != same product unless multivariate and independently replicated
